first_impression.reaction: Googled 'greece wedding packages' because we've got two Greek quotes and they don't line up. The first paragraph tells me the thing I already suspected: same title, different wedding. No 'turquoise waters' fluff. Went straight to the FAQ like I always do, then the 'What packages often leave out' section, because that's where the catch lives. Then the ten-point checklist, which I'd basically copy into my spreadsheet. It names the catches itself: items you can't swap, minimum room blocks, fees outside the package, an old brochure. My problem is a booking link before any of that, and an advisor 'route' that gets no trade-off when the other three do.

journey.quote: Two package documents from two Greek resorts can share a title and describe quite different weddings.
journey.reaction: Right. That's my actual problem, and they say it before trying to sell me anything.

journey.quote: If you already hold two quotes and want them read side by side, book a Wedded Concierge consultation.
journey.reaction: Four bullet points in and I'm being asked to book. You haven't shown me one venue yet. Put this after the checklist, where you've earned it.

journey.quote: Not published: whether the government fees Melenos attends to sit inside or outside its costing.
journey.reaction: They admit the gap rather than guessing. Good. That tells me to ask, and it makes me trust the parts that are filled in.

journey.quote: Its weddings page still links the 2025-2026 brochure, so ask for the terms that apply to a 2027 date.
journey.reaction: Dated terms with a shelf life. I can check that, and they're telling me it might be out of date.

journey.quote: An offer of that kind rewards the size of the celebration, so read it against the spend it asks for.
journey.reaction: That's the catch on a 'complimentary night', pointed out by the people who'd benefit from me not noticing it.

journey.quote: On Crete, the published packages are the most detailed in Greece: Elounda Beach, the Elounda Collection, Nana Princess, Abaton and Euphoria each set out inclusions on paper.
journey.reaction: The page backs it up with the venues it lists, but 'most detailed in Greece' is a claim about every venue in the country. Say 'in this guide' and I don't have to wonder.

journey.quote: The brochure it links dates from 2022, so ask Lagonissi for the current package before you compare it with anything.
journey.reaction: Another date, another warning. This is the sort of thing I'd normally only find by checking it myself.

journey.quote: The gaps in a package are rarely hidden. They sit in the conditions, the additional services list and the line that says "subject to availability".
journey.reaction: Exactly where I'd look. A section on what's NOT included is the reason I'd bookmark this.

journey.quote: Abaton's 2025-2026 terms say packages do not include accommodation and are valid with a minimum booking of 10 rooms for two nights and at least 20 reception guests.
journey.reaction: Hard numbers and a condition I'd want to know before I fall for a venue. This is what 'proof, not promises' looks like.

journey.quote: Euphoria's packages "are complete packages, and their items are not interchangeable", with no refund or alternative for a service you skip.
journey.reaction: Quoting the venue's own terms on the catch. No spin.

journey.section: Venue package, planner or building your own
journey.quote: Wedded Concierge is a fourth route. Your Wedded Advisor is a single point of contact who plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world.
journey.reaction: The other three routes each get an honest trade-off: less flexibility, one more contract, more paperwork. Yours gets none. And 'payments' makes me ask straight away: does my money go through you, and do you take a cut from the venue?

journey.section: How to compare two quotes like for like
journey.quote: If one quote answers a point and the other is silent, the silent one is not cheaper. It is unfinished.
journey.reaction: Best line on the page. And the ten questions above it are going straight into my spreadsheet.

journey.section: For Australian couples: currency, deposits and insurance
journey.quote: Start with the currency. Is the quote in euro, and will the deposit and the balance be invoiced in the same currency? Which items, such as municipal or church fees, are paid locally and separately? Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD.
journey.reaction: Good questions, then the 'quotes in AUD' line again. That's the fourth time. If the venue bills in euro and you quote me in AUD, whose exchange rate is that, and is there a margin in it?

journey.section: For Australian couples: currency, deposits and insurance
journey.quote: Basic medical-only policies usually don't cover cancellation costs, and credit card insurance often covers fewer situations and usually has to be activated.
journey.reaction: Dated Smartraveller advice, and it's the sort of thing that bites people. Useful for my parents too.

journey.quote: Rarely in the sense most couples mean.
journey.reaction: A straight answer to 'all inclusive?' with three named exclusions behind it. That's what I want from an FAQ.

journey.quote: A marriage made overseas is usually recognised in Australia if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law, and a lawyer can confirm validity.
journey.reaction: The question is 'Can Australians legally marry in Greece?' and the answer starts with recognition back home. I had to read it twice to work out whether that's a yes. Lead with the direct answer.

journey.quote: Euphoria and Abaton sell complete packages whose items are not interchangeable.
journey.reaction: That's about swapping items, not about bringing my own photographer. The question was whether I can bring suppliers, and for those two I still don't know.

journey.section: Compare your shortlist with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Right signal. Still doesn't tell me how the fee is worked out or whether the venues pay you too.

unanswered_questions: Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from any of these venues, and does that affect which ones the Wedded Advisor recommends?
How is the Wedded Concierge fee calculated and what exactly does it cover?
When the Wedded Advisor 'quotes in AUD', whose exchange rate is used and is there a margin on the conversion?
Does money for venues and vendors pass through Wedded Wonderland ('plans ... payments'), and if so how is it held?
Is the first consultation free, and what do I get from it?
Can I bring my own photographer or florist to Euphoria or Abaton?
Is there a real Greek wedding with the actual budget I can look at?

turn_offs_found.quote: If you already hold two quotes and want them read side by side, book a Wedded Concierge consultation.
turn_offs_found.why: It sits straight after four bullet points and before a single venue or condition. The page's evidence is genuinely good, so asking me to book before showing any of it makes the sale look like the point.

turn_offs_found.quote: Wedded Concierge is a fourth route. Your Wedded Advisor is a single point of contact who plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world.
turn_offs_found.why: Every other route in that section gets a named trade-off. The one you sell gets only upsides. That's the exact moment a sceptic notices whose page this is, and it undercuts the honesty of the three paragraphs above it.

turn_offs_found.quote: On Crete, the published packages are the most detailed in Greece: Elounda Beach, the Elounda Collection, Nana Princess, Abaton and Euphoria each set out inclusions on paper.
turn_offs_found.why: A country-wide superlative resting on the venues in one article. It's probably fair for this list, but 'in Greece' claims more than the page shows, and superlatives are what I check first.

would_share_with: My fiancee, the ten-question checklist, to send to both venues
My dad, the currency, deposit and insurance section

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, compare your shortlist with a Wedded Advisor, or return to our curated Greece wedding collection.
cta_reaction.why: The page earned it: catches named, dates on terms, blanks admitted, the venues' own exclusions quoted. It's the most useful thing I've read on Greek packages. What holds me back is the same question I ask every planner: do you take a cut from the venue, and is there a margin in the AUD quote? The fee-in-writing line helps but doesn't answer that, and the Concierge 'route' being the only one without a downside makes me more careful, not less.

top_3_changes: Move the first Wedded Concierge link out of the Key takeaways and below the ten-question checklist, so the first ask comes after the evidence.

Give the Wedded Concierge 'fourth route' the same honest trade-off line the other three routes get, and cut the repeated 'quotes in AUD' line from four mentions to one or two. (Commission, fee model and AUD conversion detail would also help, but those are deferred business details, so nice-to-have.)

Tighten two FAQ answers and one claim: open 'Can Australians legally marry in Greece?' with a direct answer before the recognition point, make 'Can we bring our own planner or suppliers?' actually answer the supplier question for Euphoria and Abaton (or say it's not published), and change 'the most detailed in Greece' to 'the most detailed in this guide'.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ and exclusions first, looked for catches, superlatives, fee model, commissions and currency margin
No invented brand facts; fee, commission, AUD conversion, payment handling and first-call details placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (image slots, fact tags, CTA marker) ignored
Title, deferred business details and absence of prices not flagged as must-fix; no requests for sourcing or 'how we know' lines

open_questions.question: The 'fourth route' paragraph is the only option without a trade-off. Fixing it is a copy-balance change, not a fee disclosure. Should the writer add a trade-off line this round, or does it wait for the deferred business details?

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'greece wedding packages' holding two Greek quotes and comparing three planners, hence top relevance.
No prices on the page is by design and not penalised.
Title is person-set and deferred, so not assessed.
